text.p: Here are highlights from Polish newspapers this morning.
- Solidarity trade unions will challenge the new narrowly passed constitution in the Supreme Court due to alleged violations of the elections law, Solidarity said.

- Poland will be invited to join NATO at the pact's summit in Madrid in July this year, a NATO diplomat who declined to be named said. None of the pact's foreign ministers present at the meeting yesterday opposed Poland's future membership.

- The US JP Morgan investment bank, Sweden's Sparbanken and the Swiss Zurich Group insurers will all buy up to 30 percent of shares in the privatised Bank Handlowy. Individually the investors will be allowed to buy up to 10 percent stakes in the bank, Handlowy said.

- The listed ComputerLand computer systems' integrator and the JTT Computer hardware maker have agreed to cooperate in production, promotion and sale of the Patriot Line network systems to be bought by government institutions and big corporations, the firms' presidents Tomasz Sielicki and Tomasz Czechowicz said.

- The Bank Gdanski shareholders will receive 11 shares of the listed Bank Inicjatyw Gospodarczych (BIG) in return for their shares following the planned merger of the two banks, the general shareholders meeting of BIG bank decided.
- Poland's two biggest petrol refineries, Petrochemia Plock and Petrochemia Gdansk are planning to increase fuel prices by 0.03 zloty due to the recent excise tax increase, the refineries said.

- The Warsaw Provincial Court has ruled against the sale of shares in the privatised Ruch press distribution chain before the conclusion of legal proceeding in the HDS Wydawcy Prasy versus the treasury ministry case, the court said.

- The International Finance Corporation (IFC) will put off its investment in the Powszechny Zaklad Ubezpieczen (PZU) Poland biggest insurance firm as the company's privatisation and restructuring have been halted, IFC's representative Hugh Stevenson said.
- The Lodz-based Chemiskor leather processing plant is considering a joint venture with the Hoechst and Clariant concerns to build a new leather dye plant, a source who declined to be named said.

- The PZU insurer has attracted a group of investors ready to buy up to 600 million zlotys worth of B-series shares which will enable PZU to reach the required solvency ratio, a source who declined to be named said. NOTE - Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
